title: Use chute-closure fullness behavior and exchange timing targets to interpret exchange performance issues
summary: Chute closure is described as a fullness-driven behavior: the chute closes when the chute is full (not simply when both AGVs are in the station). The source also provides exchange timing targets and a threshold concept: stage exchanges before reaching 80% fullness, with a goal of median 8-second exchange time and a floor of 6.7 seconds. If exchanges/tipping are slow, chutes can close, and exchange time can extend into the minutes area after closure.
when_to_use: Use when you need to interpret why chute closure is occurring and how exchange timing targets relate to avoiding chute closure during AGV/tipper exchanges.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Interpret observed chute-closure timing and exchange performance against the source’s fullness-based chute closure rule and the exchange timing targets (median 8 seconds; floor 6.7 seconds) and the “before 80%” staging concept.
access_or_tools_needed: Training video segment transcript (00:28:37.000 to 00:32:10.000) for chute closure and timing targets

visual_references.description: Frame/transcript segment that states chute closure is fullness-driven and provides the exchange timing targets (median 8 seconds; floor 6.7 seconds) and the “before 80%” staging concept, plus the impact of closing the chute first (exchange time into minutes).

steps.title: Apply the chute-closure rule: chute closes when the chute is full
steps.purpose: To correctly attribute chute closure to fullness rather than to the mere presence of both AGVs in the station.
steps.instruction: When you observe chute closure behavior during exchanges, interpret it using the source rule: the chute gets closed when the chute is full, not when both AGVs are in the station.
steps.expected_result: Your explanation for the observed chute closure is based on chute fullness (full chute triggers closure), rather than on whether both AGVs were in the station.
steps.healthy_condition: Chute closure timing can be explained as occurring after the chute becomes full, consistent with the source’s fullness-driven rule.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reconcile chute closure timing with a fullness-driven explanation (e.g., closure occurs without the chute reaching a full condition per the source’s model).

actions.label: Use fullness-based closure interpretation
actions.exact_action: Use the source rule for chute closure: chute gets closed when the chute is full, not when both of them are in the station.

stop_or_escalate_if: If chute closure timing does not align with the fullness-based explanation, escalate for deeper investigation beyond this segment.

source_evidence.evidence_text: “The chute gets closed when the the the chute is full, not when both of them are in this in the station or it's both.”

steps.title: Link slow exchange/tipping to eventual chute closure
steps.purpose: To predict the system behavior when exchanges are not keeping up (e.g., tipping not quick enough).
steps.instruction: If exchange performance is slow (for example, tipping is not happening quickly enough), interpret that shoots/chutes will eventually close as everything gets full.
steps.expected_result: You can connect the observed exchange slowness to eventual chute closure as a consequence of the chute reaching full conditions.
steps.healthy_condition: Exchange performance is sufficient to prevent the chute from reaching the full condition that triggers closure.
steps.failure_condition: Exchange performance is insufficient, and chute closure occurs as the chute becomes full.

actions.label: Interpret slowness as a cause of eventual closure
actions.exact_action: If you don't run the tippers, all shoots will eventually close on their own because everything gets full.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the observed behavior does not match the “slow tipping/exchange leads to eventual closure” model, escalate for deeper investigation beyond this segment.

source_evidence.evidence_text: “if let's say you're not keeping u with exchanges or like let's say you're not tipping quick enough, right? Shoots will close. Like if you don't run the tippers, all shoots will eventually close on their own because everything gets full.”

steps.title: Use the exchange staging threshold concept: exchange before 80%
steps.purpose: To interpret whether exchange timing is being managed early enough to avoid chute closure.
steps.instruction: When interpreting exchange performance, apply the source’s threshold concept: stage for an exchange and complete it before hitting 80% fullness.
steps.expected_result: Your interpretation includes whether exchanges were completed before the 80% fullness threshold concept described by the source.
steps.healthy_condition: Exchanges occur before the chute reaches the “80%” point described by the source, providing more control and preventing chute closure.
steps.failure_condition: Exchanges occur too late (after the chute reaches the threshold concept), leading to chute closure before the exchange completes.

actions.label: Check timing against the 80% staging concept
actions.exact_action: Our thresholds we stage for an exchange and before we hit that 80%, we've already done the exchange.

stop_or_escalate_if: If chute closure occurs despite exchanges being expected to complete before 80%, escalate for deeper investigation beyond this segment.

source_evidence.evidence_text: “Ideally, the way it works is our thresholds we stage for an exchange and before we hit that 80%, we've already done the exchange.”

steps.title: Frame expectations with exchange timing targets (median 8 seconds; floor 6.7 seconds)
steps.purpose: To interpret exchange performance using the source’s timing targets and to distinguish normal vs degraded exchange behavior.
steps.instruction: When interpreting exchange timing, use the source’s targets: goal is a median 8-second exchange time and the floor is 6.7 seconds.
steps.expected_result: You can state whether the observed exchange timing is consistent with the source’s median 8-second goal and 6.7-second floor.
steps.healthy_condition: Exchange timing aligns with the source’s goal (median 8 seconds) and does not fall below the source’s floor (6.7 seconds).
steps.failure_condition: Exchange timing is significantly slower than the source’s targets, consistent with exchanges not being completed before chute closure.

actions.label: Compare observed exchange timing to targets
actions.exact_action: Our goal is like a median 8 second exchange time. And so our bottom, like our floor is like 6.7 seconds.

stop_or_escalate_if: If exchange timing does not match the source’s targets and chute closure behavior cannot be explained by the fullness/threshold model, escalate for deeper investigation beyond this segment.

source_evidence.evidence_text: “our goal is like a median 8 second exchange time. And so our, our bottom, like our floor is like 6.7 seconds.”

steps.title: Explain the impact when chute closes before the exchange completes
steps.purpose: To interpret why exchange time can become much longer after chute closure.
steps.instruction: If you determine the chute closed before the exchange, anticipate the source-described impact: exchange time can extend into the minutes area after closing the chute, picking it up, and then exchanging.
steps.expected_result: Your interpretation explains prolonged exchange time as a downstream effect of chute closure occurring before the exchange.
steps.healthy_condition: Exchange completes before chute closure, so exchange time remains near the source’s targets rather than extending into minutes.
steps.failure_condition: Chute closure occurs first, and exchange time extends into the minutes area after closure and subsequent pick-up/exchange.

actions.label: Attribute long exchange time to chute-closure-first sequence
actions.exact_action: Because if you close the chute, then pick it up, then exchange it, then the exchange time's going to be, you know, in the minutes area.

stop_or_escalate_if: If chute closure timing and exchange timing do not follow the source-described sequence (closure first leading to minutes-area exchange time), escalate for deeper investigation beyond this segment.

source_evidence.evidence_text: “Because if you close the chute, then pick it up, then exchange it, then the exchange time's going to be, you know, in the minutes area.”

success_criteria: You can explain chute closure timing using the fullness-based rule (chute closes when full, not when both AGVs are in station).
You can relate observed exchange slowness to eventual chute closure (e.g., not tipping quick enough).
You can apply the source’s threshold concept (exchange before 80%) and timing targets (median 8 seconds; floor 6.7 seconds).
If chute closure occurs first, you can explain why exchange time extends into minutes area.
healthy_conditions: Chute closure is avoided because exchanges are completed before the chute reaches the source’s threshold concept (before 80%).
Exchange timing is consistent with the source’s goal (median 8 seconds) and floor (6.7 seconds).
failure_conditions: Chute closure occurs and cannot be explained by the chute-fullness rule.
Exchange timing is slow enough that chute closure occurs before exchange completion.
Observed exchange timing extends into minutes area without a chute-closure-first sequence that matches the source model.
escalation_guidance: If chute closure timing does not align with the fullness-based explanation, escalate for deeper investigation beyond this training segment.
missing_details: The packet does not provide live system UI/API fields to measure chute fullness, chute-closed timestamps, or exchange timing directly; it only provides the interpretation rules and timing targets from the training segment.
